title: Adobe OAuth Web App client secret in a Basic Authorization envelope
summary: A synthetic encoded credential after the Basic scheme in the Authorization header of a token request, a refresh request and a revocation request. The encoded value is the base64 of a synthetic client id and a synthetic client secret joined by a colon.
rationale: Adobe documents that a confidential client (the OAuth Web App credential) presents Authorization: Basic Base64(clientId:clientSecret) on the authorization-code token request, the refresh request and the revocation request (contract claim web-app-client-secret-basic-authorization). The secret exists only inside the encoded credential, so the extent is the whole encoded token, not a decoded secret-only span; the same convention is used for the other Basic-envelope Cases of this repository. Adobe states no prefix, alphabet or width for the secret. Whether a decoded header is in scope is the contract's open question basic-header-is-derived-form and is not decided here beyond the encoded form.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the encoded credential after the Basic scheme in a token, refresh or revocation request of a confidential Adobe client is treated as a credential and covered whole. Adobe documents the Basic envelope of client id and client secret on those requests (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: The authorization parameter is required for confidential clients as Authorization: Basic Base64(clientId:clientSecret) on the access-token and refresh requests (the request example for the OAuth Web App credential carries only the Authorization header and the code or refresh_token); the revocation request takes the same header for OAuth Web and OAuth WebApp credentials; client_id is required for public clients.
